dataset: Merdith et al. (2021) continuous full-plate motion model, 1 Ga to present
author: A. S. Merdith and co-authors; EarthByte Group, University of Sydney
citation: Merdith, A. S., Williams, S. E., Collins, A. S., Tetley, M. G., Mulder, J. A., Blades, M. L., Young, A., Armistead, S. E., Cannon, J., Zahirovic, S., and Müller, R. D., 2021. Extending full-plate tectonic models into deep time: Linking the Neoproterozoic and the Phanerozoic. Earth-Science Reviews, 214, 103477.

license.name: Creative Commons Attribution 3.0 Unported
license.statement: Data by the EarthByte Group is licensed under a Creative Commons Attribution 3.0 Unported License.
license.note: Attribution and citation are required. Unlike the PALEOMAP maps this project also uses, publishing derived work on a website needs no further consent.

usage: Local research reference. Extracted members are verified against the hashes below; nothing is served until a publication decision is recorded like the one in deploy/deploy.toml.

members.name: 1000_0_rotfile_Merdith_et_al.rot
members.role: rotation model: total reconstruction poles per moving/fixed plate pair

members.name: shapes_coastlines_Merdith_et_al_v2.gpmlz
members.role: present-day coastlines with plate IDs, mainly meaningful for the past 400 Ma

members.name: shapes_continents.gpml
members.role: continental shapes with plate IDs, for the past 1 Ga

members.name: shapes_static_polygons_Merdith_et_al.gpml
members.role: static polygons: which plate ID a present-day location belongs to

members.name: ReadMe_SM2.txt
members.role: the authors' own description, including what the model is not suitable for

limitations: The authors state the model is in a purely palaeomagnetic reference frame and is unsuitable for Pacific hotspot kinematics or for analyses shorter than 5 Ma. Longitude in the Precambrian is weakly constrained by palaeomagnetism alone.
